subtype: Letters and poetry for meaning and memory [Expressing]
passage:
Dear Pankaj,
I still can't believe Uncle is gone. I wanted to call, but I didn't trust my voice, so I'm writing, and I hope you will keep this for the days when the phone stops ringing. I remember the summer your father taught us to fix the bicycle chain and laughed when I got grease on my ears. I remember him arriving with sweets on every exam result day, even mine. I don't have wise words. I only want you to know he made me feel welcome in your home. If you'd like company, or silence, or someone to sit with you on the terrace, I'm here.
With love,
Hrithik

qa.q: What did Uncle bring on exam result days?
What was Hrithik feeling when deciding to write instead of call?
qa.a: Hrithik was grieving and unsteady, not trusting a voice on the phone, and writing made it possible to say what was felt.

qa.q: What makes the letter comforting for Pankaj?
qa.a: It shares real memories and offers company, silence or a seat on the terrace without demanding a reply.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel rereading the letter later?
qa.a: It may comfort Pankaj, since the letter can be kept, though it may also bring the grief back. 🤍

grounding: A young adult writes a condolence letter with memories and an open offer, words that can be kept and reread.

subtype: Letters and poetry for meaning and memory [Expressing]
passage: People ask me why I write letters to myself. I'm Raghav. Two years ago, the night before I left for my first job in another city, Hemant, my roommate, said, "Write something. You'll want it later." So I wrote a letter to myself, five years ahead. I put in the fear, the chai stains on my notebook, the promise that I'd call my parents every Sunday. I sealed it and gave it to Hemant to keep. Last month, on a rough day, I asked for it back early. I read it on the balcony and cried a bit, because the person in that letter was so hopeful. Then I sealed it again. It isn't a great poem. But it says what I felt, and it stays put.

qa.q: What was Raghav feeling when reading the letter on the balcony?
qa.a: Raghav was moved and a bit sad, crying a little at how hopeful Raghav's earlier self was.

qa.q: What could Raghav do with the letter now?
qa.a: Raghav can keep it sealed until the time first chosen, or add a short reply for the future self.

qa.q: How might Hemant see the letter?
qa.a: As something precious Hemant was trusted with, since Raghav gave it to Hemant to keep and later asked for it back.

grounding: A young adult writes a letter to a future self to mark feelings, and the kept words carry comfort and permanence.
